d: Race condition in CAS-based algorithms where value changes from A to B and back to A between check and update, fooling CAS into succeeding incorrectly; solved with tagged pointers or hazard tracking.
Memory ordering semantics ensuring all subsequent loads/stores cannot be reordered before the acquire operation; used for lock acquisition, reading a flag after volatile write.
Multiple threads competing simultaneously for the same contested lock after waking; the collision created by the wake spike.
Formula limiting parallel speedup by the serial fraction of computation; speedup <= 1 / (serial_fraction + parallel_fraction / num_threads); motivates minimization of synchronized serial sections.
Weak memory model used by ARM processors where memory operations may be reordered extensively unless explicitly ordered by barriers; most permissive of common architectures.
Compare-and-swap operation atomically loading a value, comparing it to an expected value, and storing a new value only if they matched, returning whether the swap occurred.
C++11/C11 atomic operation attempting to replace expected value with desired; returns boolean indicating success; on failure, expected is updated with actual value for retry loops.
Atomic operation that reads the current value of a variable and writes a new value in a single indivisible step, returning the old value.
Operation appearing indivisible to other threads; either hardware-supported single instruction atomics or software-implemented atomic primitives using CAS loops.
Zero-based counter tracking how many consecutive failed lock acquisition attempts have occurred since last success.
Scaling factor (commonly 2.0) that multiplies the current delay on each failed acquisition attempt to produce the next delay interval.
Primitive blocking threads until all threads in a set reach the barrier point; threads proceed only after the group is complete; used in fork-join and bulk-synchronous parallelism.
Initial wait time in nanoseconds or microseconds before the first lock acquisition retry; the starting point of the exponential schedule.
Semaphore with counter restricted to 0 or 1; functions like a mutex but without ownership semantics; can be signaled by non-owner thread.
Classic synchronization problem with fixed-size buffer between producers and consumers; requires empty/full conditions and mutual exclusion; solution uses semaphores or monitors.
Property requiring that after a thread requests entry to a critical section, there is a bound on the number of other threads allowed to enter before the requester.
The invocation or mechanism that triggers wake_all_semantics; e.g., pthread_cond_broadcast, event_group.set_all, NotifyAll in a monitor.

A relaxed atomic operation is not a thread fence; unlike atomic_thread_fence with memory_order_seq_cst, a relaxed operation imposes no memory barrier that would establish synchronization between threads.

Standard C11 specification defining memory orderings: memory_order_relaxed, memory_order_consume, memory_order_acquire, memory_order_release, memory_order_acq_rel, memory_order_seq_cst; defines happens-before and synchronizes-with relations.
Placement of data structures on memory boundaries matching cache line size, typically 64 bytes, preventing false sharing between adjacent data.
Protocol ensuring that multiple caches sharing a memory location present a consistent view; MESI, MOESI, MESIF protocols maintain coherence across CPU cores.

Performance anti-pattern where threads on different cores repeatedly invalidate each other's cache line, causing excessive coherency traffic; often caused by false sharing or poorly designed data structures.
Relaxed operations respect intra-thread causality (program order) but do not guarantee inter-thread causality; this boundary defines the scope of what relaxed_atomicity guarantees.
Communication primitive from Communicating Sequential Processes model; send and receive operations synchronize producers and consumers; implementations include Go channels, Clojure core.async.
Queued lock using a linked list of nodes with spinning on predecessor's flag; provides scalability and fairness similar to MCS but different cache behavior.

Property that each memory location has a single globally visible value at any instant; distinct from consistency, coherence governs single-location semantics while consistency governs multi-location ordering.
Atomic instruction comparing a value with expected and swaps only if equal; fundamental building block for lock-free algorithms; ABA problem may require additional solutions.
Directive preventing the compiler from reordering memory operations across the barrier; does not emit hardware instructions but prevents compiler optimization from causing races.
Java class implementing Future with completion callbacks, chaining, and composition; supports thenApply, thenCompose, exceptionally; enables non-blocking asynchronous pipelines.
Primitive enabling a thread to wait for a condition to become true; must be used with a mutex; wait atomically releases the mutex and blocks; notify/notify_all wake waiting threads.
The specific use of a condition variable with broadcast to notify waiting threads; a primary vector for thundering herd emergence in monitor-based code.
Operating system operation saving one thread's state and restoring another's; involves kernel transition, register saves, TLB invalidation; cost motivates lock-free and per-thread data designs.
One-time barrier initialized with a count; threads decrement count on completion; barrier opens when count reaches zero; cannot be reused.
General semaphore with non-negative integer counter allowing multiple concurrent accesses; used for resource pooling and bounded work distribution.
C++11 and later standard library memory model supporting atomic operations with configurable ordering; provides std::atomic with memory_order enum values matching C11 semantics.
Other threads may observe relaxed operations in any order relative to each other; there is no single total order visible to all threads as there is with sequentially_consistent.
The computed wait interval for the current retry iteration; derived from base_delay multiplied by backoff_multiplier raised to the iteration count, then capped by delay_ceiling.
Barrier implementation that resets after all threads pass; supports configurable thread count and optional action executed when barrier breaks.
Specific concurrent access where at least one access is a write, accesses are to same memory location, and accesses are not properly synchronized; undefined behavior in C11/C++11.
Liveness failure where two or more threads wait indefinitely for conditions held by each other; occurs with circular wait, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and mutual exclusion.

Design strategies eliminating one of the four Coffman conditions: no circular wait (lock ordering), hold-and-wait (acquire all at once), preemption (non-preemptive resources), mutual exclusion (lock-free alternatives).
Jitter strategy where each thread computes delay = random.uniform(min_delay, previous_delay * 3); history-dependent decorrelation reduces coordinated retry waves.
First correct two-process mutual exclusion algorithm achieving progress under sequential consistency; combines turn-taking with turn variable; also fails under relaxed memory ordering.
Upper bound cap on the computed delay; prevents unbounded growth of wait times when contention persists across many iterations.
Classic deadlock problem with N philosophers at circular table needing both adjacent forks; demonstrates resource ordering, deadlock avoidance, and starvation-free synchronization design.

The closed interval [min_delay, previous_delay times decorrelation_factor] from which the uniform random sample is drawn to compute the next current_delay; bounds the worst-case wait while allowing history-dependent growth.
The multiplicative constant (commonly 3.0) that scales previous_delay to produce the upper bound of the sampling range; governs how aggressively the wait distribution spreads across retry iterations.

The accumulated sequence of previous_delay values maintained per thread that enables history-dependent decorrelation; each thread derives its next upper bound from its own history rather than a shared schedule.

Lower bound of the uniform sampling range in decorrelated jitter; typically derived from base_delay and serves as the floor below which no wait interval may fall, ensuring at least a minimal pause before retry.
The computed wait interval from the immediately prior backoff iteration on the same thread; serves as the history anchor from which the upper bound of the new sampling range is derived.
The uniform random draw within the bounding range that produces the new current_delay value; the randomness decorrelates this thread's retry timing from concurrent threads.
Per-thread isolation of history_state and current_delay computation; ensures no shared counter or schedule exists across competing threads, preventing coordinated retry waves.
The emergent property that decorrelated jitter reduces the probability of simultaneous retries among competing threads; achieved through per-thread history-dependent ranges that diverge over time.
Memory reclamation scheme batching deletions into epochs; threads must wait for active epochs to complete before reclaiming protected memory; balances throughput and safety.
Jitter strategy computing delay = base_delay / 2 + random.uniform(0, base_delay / 2); ensures wait never falls below half the nominal delay.
The use of an event or manual-reset signaling object that wakes all waiters; a primary vector distinct from condition-variable-based triggers.
Contention management strategy backing off exponentially after failed lock acquisition; reduces bus traffic and collision; common in spinlock and CAS-based algorithm implementations.
Exponential backoff applied post-wake to decorrelate retry timing of competing threads; reduces acquisition_collision frequency.
A thread woken from a blocking wait that immediately discovers it cannot acquire the resource and must re-block or retry; the atomic waste unit of a thundering herd.
Performance problem where unrelated variables sharing a cache line cause cache coherency traffic when one is modified; threads updating different variables contend due to line-level sharing.

Placing a release fence after a relaxed store does not retroactively give the store release semantics; fences only constrain operations that follow them, not operations that precede them in program order.
Atomic operation returning old value while atomically incrementing memory location; used for counters, ticket distribution, and implementing certain lock-free structures.
Parallelism pattern where work recursively splits into subtasks that join at barriers; implementations like Java ForkJoinFramework provide efficient work stealing for divide-conquer algorithms.
Jitter strategy selecting a uniform random value in the range [0, current_delay]; maximizes desynchronization at the cost of potentially very short waits.
Fast userspace mutex kernel-assisted synchronization; userspace spinning first, then syscall to kernel for wait/wake; basis for most Linux threading primitives.
Concurrency pattern decoupling value computation from access; Future represents pending result, Promise provides completion mechanism; enables asynchronous composition.

A fundamental ordering relation in memory models defining that if operation A happens-before operation B, then A's effects are visible to B; forms the basis for reasoning about program correctness in concurrent settings.
CPU-supported transactional execution using cache hierarchies to track conflicts; Intel TSX and IBM Blue Gene/Q implementations; aborts on cache conflict or unsupported instruction.
Memory reclamation technique where each thread publishes dangerous pointers to globally accessible locations; memory cannot be reclaimed while referenced by any hazard pointer.
CPU or compiler reordering of memory operations for performance while preserving single-thread correctness; can violate programmer expectations in concurrent code without proper barriers.
Within a single thread, the thread still observes its own relaxed operations in program order; this total order is local to the thread and not shared.
Hardware queue holding pending invalidation requests for cache lines; entries must be drained before a core can ensure it has exclusive ownership of a cache line.
Java Memory Model (JSR-133) specifying happens-before guarantees for synchronized blocks, volatile fields, thread start/join; defines ordering guarantees for concurrent Java programs.
Randomized variance introduced into the computed delay to decorrelate competing threads and mitigate thundering-herd synchronization on lock release.
N-thread mutual exclusion algorithm providing first-come-first-served ordering; uses ticket numbers; correct under sequential consistency but requires adaptation for weak memory models.
Correctness criterion requiring each operation appear to execute atomically at some point between invocation and response; composable property essential for concurrent object specifications.
Failure where threads continuously respond to each other without making progress; distinguishable from deadlock by active state; often result of excessive collision avoidance.
Phenomenon in weak memory models where a load may observe a store from a different thread that happens later in global order, enabling patterns impossible under SC.

Under relaxed ordering, a thread may read a value it will later write (load buffering) because relaxed operations do not prohibit such behavior unlike sequentially consistent or release-acquire patterns.
Pair of instructions for software atomic operations: LL reads atomically, SC writes only if no intervening store occurred; used on ARM, PowerPC; avoids ABA problem inherent to CAS.
Optimization technique using HTM or CAS to execute critical sections without holding the lock when no conflict occurs; combines performance of no-locking with safety of mutual exclusion.
Progress guarantee where system-wide progress is always made; at least one thread completes an operation in finite steps regardless of other thread interference.
Queued lock where each waiting thread spins on a locally-owned node linked into a queue; cache-friendly with only O(1) bus traffic per lock acquisition; named after Mellor-Crummey and Scott.

Operation by which a thread obtains the lock; spins polling its own qnode.locked field until false; returns only after predecessor has released and cleared the flag; no shared atomic variable is spun on.
Operation appending a thread-local qnode to the queue tail; atomically CASes qnode into tail; on CAS failure, completes the predecessor's link and retries; ensures FIFO acquisition order.
Property guaranteed by MCS queue structure; lock acquisition order matches the order of enqueue operations; provides fairness without centralized ticket counters.

Backoff resolution protocol during failed enqueue CAS; the thread that lost the CAS follows the discovered pointer chain to complete the linking work of the winner before retrying its own append; prevents starvation under high contention.

Performance property of MCS; each waiter spins on its own thread-local qnode in its own cache line; eliminates cache-line ping-ponging between spinning threads; reduces bus traffic to O(1) per lock handoff.
Thread-local queue node containing locked flag and successor pointer; must be cache-aligned and allocated per-thread to enable local spinning without shared contention.
Boolean field in qnode; spinning thread reads this; set true on enqueue and cleared false by predecessor upon release; default true indicates lock not yet released.
Pointer field in qnode referencing successor qnode; null until predecessor links this node; spinning thread polls this to detect when it has been chained into the queue.

Operation by which a thread releases the lock; sets own qnode.locked to false to unblock spinning successor; if successor exists in qnode.next, responsibility transfers to successor's own spin; cache-friendly O(1) handoff.
Atomic shared pointer to the last enqueued qnode; initialized null; updated via CAS during enqueue; represents the lock acquisition frontier.
Sub-protocol when release finds no successor yet linked; thread performing release or a helper spins on qnode.next until non-null; ensures no lock holder exits before its successor is queued.
Instruction or hardware mechanism that prevents reordering of memory operations across the barrier; ensures visibility and ordering of loads and stores relative to the barrier point.
Synonym for memory barrier; hardware instruction enforcing visibility and ordering constraints on memory operations across the fence; variations include full fence, store fence, load fence.
Memory ordering barrier ensuring all loads and stores after the barrier in program order cannot be reordered before it, synchronizing with release stores.
C11/C++11 ordering enforcing data-dependency ordering; subsequent operations dependent on the consumed value maintain ordering but other operations may reorder; often optimized to acquire.
C11/C++11 memory ordering that only guarantees atomicity of the operation with no ordering constraints relative to other operations; allows all reorderings.

The indivisibility guarantee that a relaxed atomic operation completes as a single indivisible step; no intermediate state is observable by other threads during the operation, scoped to the specific atomic variable being read or written.

The property that each atomic variable maintains its own independent coherence order but this order is not coordinated with coherence orders of other variables; operations on separate variables are totally unordered with respect to each other.

The undefined timing of when a relaxed load obtains its value; a load may observe any value from the modification order up to that point, with no guarantee about when the load's value becomes visible to other threads.

The per-variable constraint that each atomic variable still has a well-defined modification order agreed upon by all threads, even though relaxed operations on different variables are unconstrained relative to each other.

The defining property that relaxed operations impose zero ordering constraints relative to any other operations on any memory location; no happens-before or synchronizes-with relationship is established with respect to other threads.

The absence of any synchronization relationship; relaxed operations do not participate in the synchronizes-with relation and do not establish happens-before edges across thread boundaries regardless of visibility.

The within-thread ordering guarantee that within a single thread, the program order of relaxed operations is still preserved for that thread's own perspective; only cross-thread visibility and cross-variable ordering are relaxed.

The freedom to reorder relaxed operations across variable boundaries; a relaxed store may be reordered with respect to a relaxed load on a different variable, and loads may observe values in an order inconsistent with program order across different locations.
The phenomenon that relaxed stores may be buffered in store buffers and become visible to other threads in an order different from the program order of the storing thread.
The ordering contrast where acquire_semantics prevents subsequent operations from being reordered before the acquire, while memory_order_relaxed permits all such reorderings with no barrier effect.
The ordering contrast where release_semantics prevents prior operations from being reordered after the release, while memory_order_relaxed permits all such reorderings with no barrier effect.
The ordering contrast where sequentially_consistent imposes a single global total order visible to all threads, while memory_order_relaxed has no global ordering requirement across variables.
Memory ordering barrier ensuring all loads and stores before the barrier in program order cannot be reordered after it, making prior writes visible to acquiring threads.
Challenge of safely reclaiming freed memory in lock-free structures accessed concurrently; solutions include hazard pointers, RCU, epoch-based reclamation, and quiescent-state-based approaches.
Four-state cache coherency protocol: Modified (exclusive, dirty), Exclusive (exclusive, clean), Shared (shared, clean), Invalid (not present); prevents inconsistent cached data.

All relaxed atomic operations on the same atomic variable still observe a single total modification order consistent across all threads, though different threads need not agree on the relative order of operations to other variables.
High-level synchronization construct combining mutex and condition variables; object-oriented abstraction where methods acquire lock automatically; ensures serialized access to object state.
Mutual exclusion primitive providing exclusive access to a resource; supports lock/unlock operations and optionally trylock; may be recursive or not; implements critical section semantics.
Techniques including exponential backoff, random delays, or lock registry to prevent threads from repeatedly colliding on lock acquisition.
A relaxed operation neither participates in nor establishes a happens-before relationship with any other operation; operations may be reordered arbitrarily across thread boundaries.
A relaxed operation cannot synchronize-with any operation on another thread; release semantics and acquire semantics are absent, breaking the synchronizes-with chain.
Design consideration for systems with non-uniform memory access latency; thread affinity and data placement affect performance; synchronization must account for remote vs local memory access costs.
Progress guarantee where a thread completes an operation if it runs alone without interference; may starve under contention but has no blocking operations.
CPU feature executing instructions in data-dependency order rather than program order; enables utilization of unused execution units; interacts with memory ordering guarantees.
Memory model (SPARC) where stores may be reordered with respect to older stores but loads maintain program order relative to other loads and stores respect address dependencies; relaxes TSO slightly.
Two-thread mutual exclusion algorithm using shared flags and a turn variable; provides bounded waiting under sequential consistency but fails on modern weak-memory hardware without memory barriers.
Strategy of waking waiters in staggered groups rather than all at once; mitigates thundering herd by distributing acquisition collisions across time.
Java 7+ flexible barrier supporting dynamic thread registration and per-phase synchronization; threads register for each phase and wait until all registered threads complete the phase.
Weak memory model used by PowerPC/POWER processors with similar permissiveness to ARM; requires explicit barriers for many ordering guarantees.
Protocol resolving priority inversion by temporarily elevating the priority of a lock-holding low-priority thread to match the highest blocked thread.
Problem where low-priority thread blocks high-priority thread by holding a lock needed by both; typically resolved via priority inheritance protocols.
Concurrent pattern with producer threads generating work consumed by consumer threads; typically synchronized with bounded or unbounded channels/queues.
The property that program order defines a total order of operations only within a single thread; relaxed operations preserve this intra-thread order but nothing beyond it.
Behavior where program outcome depends on relative timing of interleaved operations on shared state; general term for any timing-dependent bug in concurrent programs.
Linux kernel synchronization mechanism allowing read-heavy workloads without reader locks; readers access data freely while writers make copies and schedule updates for later reclamation.
Synchronization primitive allowing multiple concurrent readers or exclusive single writer; improves read-heavy workloads but has higher overhead than simple mutex.
Synchronization problem requiring exclusive write access but concurrent read access; solutions vary in reader/writer preference, fairness, and implementation complexity.
Mutex variant permitting the same thread to acquire the lock multiple times; must be released same number of times; can hide design problems but necessary in some recursive patterns.
The sole guarantee of memory_order_relaxed: a load or store completes atomically without torn reads or torn writes; no other constraints are imposed.

The sole guarantee provided by memory_order_relaxed: the atomic variable is read and written atomically without tearing, but no ordering constraints are imposed on other operations relative to the relaxed operation.
An atomic load using memory_order_relaxed reads the current value of an atomic variable with no ordering constraints: the read may be reordered before or after non-atomic operations.

Memory model that permits more reorderings than sequential consistency; allows loads to be reordered with respect to stores, stores to be reordered with respect to stores, etc. Examples include ARM, PowerPC, and C11's relaxed ordering.

A read-modify-write operation (fetch_add, fetch_sub, compare_exchange) using memory_order_relaxed is atomic but unordered: it reads the current value, computes, and writes atomically without establishing any ordering.
An atomic store using memory_order_relaxed writes a value to an atomic variable with no ordering constraints: the store may be reordered before or after non-atomic operations.

A relaxed load does not acquire any synchronization semantics; subsequent operations in program order may be reordered before the relaxed load, in contrast to an acquire operation which prevents such reordering.
A relaxed store does not provide release semantics; prior operations in program order may be reordered after the relaxed store, in contrast to a release operation which prevents such reordering.

Relaxed operations are not part of the single total order of sequentially consistent operations; they do not participate in the global synchronization order that sequentially consistent operations establish.
Memory ordering semantics ensuring all prior loads/stores cannot be reordered after the release operation; used for lock release, writing data before a volatile flag.

A relaxed atomic operation imposes no constraints on the reordering of memory operations by either the compiler or the hardware; the operation may be reordered with any other operation including non-atomic and other atomic operations.
Synchronization primitive maintaining a counter representing available permits; P (wait/decrement) and V (signal/increment) operations; can control N concurrent accesses to a resource.
A mitigation using a semaphore with initial count N to admit at most N waiters per wake event; bounds the herd size to a configured N.
The guarantee that all threads observe the effects of a sequentially consistent operation at the same logical point in the global total order; reads observe the most recent write in the total order.

All threads observe sequentially consistent operations in the same relative order within the global total order; no thread can see operation A before operation B if B precedes A in the seq_cst total order.
A seq_cst load returns exactly the value written by some seq_cst store to the same address in the total order; it never returns a value that was never written nor a corrupted intermediate state.

A seq_cst read cannot observe a write that is ordered after it in the total order; the happens-before relationship established by seq_cst operations enforces a cutoff beyond which writes are not visible.

A seq_cst load observes the value written by the most recent seq_cst store to the same address in the global total order; no later store in the order can be the source of the observed value for this load.
During the execution of a seq_cst load or store, no intermediate memory state is visible to any thread; the operation is indivisible and appears instantaneous to all observers in the system.

If thread T1 observes thread T2's seq_cst store to address X, then T1 also observes every other seq_cst operation that precedes that store in the total order; observation is not partial or selective across the agreed sequence.

The logical position in the seq_cst global total order at which a given sequentially consistent read operation observes the effects of preceding operations; the read's visible value is determined by all operations ordered before it in the single agreed-upon total order.
The default memory ordering for std::atomic operations in C11/C++11 when no memory_order is explicitly specified; provides the strongest guarantees without requiring explicit fence code.
The explicit memory fence with sequentially consistent ordering that provides both acquire and release semantics plus additional ordering constraints to enforce the global total order.

A single total order of all sequentially consistent operations that is visible and agreed upon by all threads in the system; the interleaving point where all threads observe the same sequence of operations.
A load operation with sequentially consistent ordering carries acquire semantics; all subsequent loads and stores cannot be reordered before the seq_cst load.
A store operation with sequentially consistent ordering carries release semantics; all prior loads and stores cannot be reordered after the seq_cst store.
The property that each sequentially consistent operation appears indivisible and instantaneous to all observers; no intermediate states are visible during the operation.
Within each thread, sequentially consistent operations maintain program order; no reordering of these operations is permitted within the same thread.
The protocol by which sequentially consistent operations establish synchronization points between threads; creates a happens-before relationship across thread boundaries.

Memory model where all operations appear to execute in some total order consistent with program order on each thread; the default intuitive model where every load reads the result of the most recent store to that location in global time.
The strongest memory ordering requiring a single total order of all sequentially consistent operations visible to all threads; implied by default for std::atomic operations in C++.
Correctness criterion for transaction systems requiring equivalent to some serial execution of transactions; differs from linearizability in handling multiple operations per transaction.
A mitigation structure using a single flag, permit, or ticket to ensure only one waiter proceeds per signal; e.g., a boolean guard checked atomically with wait.
Transactional memory implemented entirely in software; threads validate read sets and write sets; higher overhead than HTM but works on any hardware; examples: TL2, DSTM.
Runtime optimization canceling or rolling back speculative work that becomes unnecessary; hardware support for HTM speculation rollback; software speculation requires careful compensation.
CPU technique executing instructions before their need is confirmed (e.g., branch prediction); rolled back on misprediction; interacts with memory ordering when speculative loads store visible data.
Lock implementation that spins in a tight loop waiting for acquisition; efficient when contention is brief but wasteful if held long; often implemented with atomic instructions.
A timer-driven phased_awakening mechanism that releases waiters in batches with fixed inter-batch delays.
Condition where a thread is perpetually denied resources needed for progress due to scheduling or contention patterns; unfair lock implementations may starve waiters.
Hardware structure buffering stores before they become visible to other cores; essential for TSO performance but creates visibility delays requiring memory barriers to manage.
A relaxed store may remain in a store buffer indefinitely before becoming visible to other threads; no fence or ordering constraint forces a flush.
Phenomenon where a store may be buffered and become visible later, allowing a subsequent load to observe a stale value while other threads see different orderings.
A relation between atomic operations in memory models where a release fence on one thread synchronizes with an acquire fence on another thread, establishing happens-before order across threads.

A relaxed atomic operation does not synchronize with any other operation; it establishes no happens-before or synchronizes-with relationship with any thread, including the thread that performed the operation.
Atomic operation setting a memory location to a value (typically 1) and returning its previous contents; basis for simple spinlock implementations.
Per-thread data storage allocating distinct instances to each thread; avoids synchronization for thread-private data; accessed efficiently without locking.
Pattern where many threads wake simultaneously from a blocking operation but only one can proceed; wasteful of resources; often avoided with wake-one semantics or phased awakening.

A retry strategy applied by awakened waiters using backoff_iteration, base_delay, and delay_ceiling to spread acquisition attempts in time, reducing contention_surge; a per-thread mitigation complementary to wake-one and phased_awakening.
A transient spike in the rate of lock or resource acquisition attempts triggered by mass wakeup, producing queue buildup and wasted retry cycles.
A degraded thread fairness condition where some members of the wait_set are repeatedly overtaken by newly arriving competitors, never acquiring the resource despite eligibility.
Application of jitter to retry delays using full_jitter, equal_jitter, or decorrelated_jitter to prevent synchronized re-attempts among awakened threads, breaking retry_coordination.
A staged wakeup strategy dividing waiters into cohorts awakened in sequence rather than simultaneously, damping the contention surge through temporal distribution.
The phenomenon where concurrently woken threads retry a failing operation in near-lockstep, reinforcing the contention surge; mitigated by jitter applied to retry delays.

A blocking operation returning without a corresponding signal, forcing waiters to re-evaluate conditions; when mass spurious wakeups occur the thundering-herd manifests even absent real notifications.
The number of threads resident in the wait_set at notification time; greater depth directly scales the severity of the thundering-herd.
A collection of threads blocked on a single synchronization point awaiting a condition; the structural prerequisite for thundering-herd because coordinated wakeup of this set is the failure mode.
A notification strategy where at most one waiter is awakened per signal, eliminating the surge by design; the canonical mitigation for thundering-herd in mutex and condition-variable implementations.
A single signal or broadcast that causes ALL members of a wait_set to transition from blocked to runnable simultaneously; the atomic cause of the thundering-herd pattern.
The ratio of awakened threads to threads that can usefully proceed; a ratio much greater than one indicates a thundering-herd inefficiency.
Fair lock implementation using atomic ticket counter where threads take a ticket number and spin-wait until their number is called; ensures FIFO ordering and prevents starvation.

Memory model used by x86/x64 processors where stores are globally ordered but may be buffered locally before becoming visible to other cores; a stronger model than ARM/PowerPC that prohibits most reorderings.
Concurrency control paradigm allowing sequences of operations to execute atomically without explicit locking; either hardware-assisted (HTM), software-only (STM), or hybrid.
C++ qualifier historically used for optimization barriers; in modern C++ standard, only provides address volatility semantics, not memory ordering; use std::atomic instead.
Java modifier ensuring visibility of writes across threads; provides acquire/release semantics on reads and writes; different from C++ volatile which lacks memory ordering guarantees.
Strongest progress guarantee requiring every thread to complete any operation in finite steps regardless of other thread interference; no starvation possible.
Blocking primitive behavior — e.g., pthread_cond_broadcast, SetEvent, or equivalent — that resumes all waiting threads rather than selecting one; the direct cause of the wake spike.
Metric: the distribution of acquisition latencies among threads woken simultaneously; wide spread indicates thundering herd while tight clustering indicates controlled awakening.
Blocking primitive behavior that resumes exactly one selected waiter per wake event; the canonical counter-pattern to wake_all_semantics.
Metric: threads woken per successful acquisition; a thundering herd has wake_ratio >> 1, ideally 1.
The acute moment of mass simultaneous thread wake-up from a blocking primitive; the event horizon of the thundering herd.
Metric: fraction of awakened threads that re-block without acquiring; directly measures the cost of a thundering herd episode.
A mitigation where the producer deposits work items into a lock-free queue and only one consumer wakes; avoids notifying all waiters entirely.
Load balancing strategy where idle threads steal work from busy threads' queues; typical in fork-join frameworks like Java ForkJoinPool; reduces contention compared to work distribution.

Multiple relaxed atomic stores to the same variable by one thread may be coalesced by the implementation; the compiler may eliminate some relaxed stores entirely if it can prove the behavior is preserved.
